column4: v1 split a donor type only when two FILE rows named the same donor path; a tests-only leaf whose production half already exists on master (M3EditDistancePlan) needs the split with one target, so v2 splits whenever MEMBER rows exist for (donor type, target) and lists the members without a MEMBER row as dropped in the anchor (here ALPHABET, the lane-table size of the replaced body)
column5: run 1: members=14 of 15, anchor "dropped members ALPHABET"

column4: binding a donor candidate method to the master owner is a declared edit, never an in-place rewrite: a BIND row names a file next to the recipe whose bytes replace the member, body_match turns FALSE, the bound column and the anchor name the member, and a BIND row that no target receives is refused
column5: run 1: bound=javaDistance body_match=FALSE; PROVENANCE.tsv bound column

column4: a bound member's bytes pass through the same own-type substitution as donor members (so a binding may name the target type freely), which means a binding file must not spell the donor type name: the first run's BIND anchor read "donor M3EditDistancePlanOracle.javaDistance"; the binding now says "donor crate method javaDistance"

the owner's refusals are not the crate's: M3EditDistancePlan admits 64x64 and 4,097-unit operands (1,048,576-unit budgets, Objects.requireNonNull), so the crate's IllegalArgumentException refusals stay in the oracle's admit (the proof domain) and are recorded as a NEC row, not as a FINDING against the owner; inside the domain the owner is checked on both lanes (shorter operand as the Myers pattern, longer operand as the DP pattern) against the DP reference

the receipt digest is owner-independent (the digest folds the DP reference distances), so the expected line of M3EditDistancePlanProofTest comes from the donor's own standalone Java run before the module build (javac --release 21 -Xlint:all -Werror of the crate file, java --java NO_LIB, 2.4 s): one module build, no second pass to learn the digest; the crate's PROOF_20261105.md carries no receipt line to compare against

surefire prints the module summary line as [WARNING] Tests run: ... when a test is skipped (this module always skips its two native-only tests), so a summary grep anchored on [INFO] finds nothing and, under set -o pipefail, ends the script after the build: verify.sh now accepts [INFO] or [WARNING] and never lets that grep end the run; the log, not the exit code, stays the authority
